text.headline: COVID-19 & American Air Travel
text.text: Key public-health and policy events alongside the passenger numbers from our own T-100 analysis of the ten largest U.S. metro areas.

text.headline: WHO Declares a Global Emergency
text.text: The World Health Organization declares COVID-19 a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, the first formal signal of a coming disruption to global travel.

text.headline: U.S. Restricts Travel From China
text.text: The United States announces restrictions on entry for most travelers who had recently been in China, an early sign that international air travel would be first to feel the shock.

text.headline: Pandemic Declared; Europe Travel Ban
text.text: The WHO declares COVID-19 a pandemic. The U.S. announces a 30-day suspension of travel from most of Europe, taking effect March 13.

text.headline: U.S. National Emergency Declared
text.text: A national emergency is declared, and states begin issuing stay-at-home orders in the following weeks. Business and leisure travel both begin their steepest collapse.

text.headline: Passenger Volume Bottoms Out
text.text: In our own data, April 2020 is the low point: the ten metro areas we studied carried only about 1.4 million passengers, down from 35.2 million in April 2019 — a 96% collapse in a single year.

text.headline: Federal Mask Mandate for Travel
text.text: A federal mandate requires masks on commercial aircraft and in transit hubs, formalizing pandemic-era travel conditions as vaccines begin rolling out nationally.

text.headline: U.S. Reopens to Vaccinated Travelers
text.text: The United States lifts pandemic-era entry restrictions for fully vaccinated international visitors, a turning point our data shows in the following year's international recovery.

text.headline: Transportation Mask Mandate Ends
text.text: A federal court ruling voids the transportation mask mandate; airlines drop the requirement the same day, symbolically closing the acute phase of the pandemic for air travel.

text.headline: "Revenge Travel" Summer
text.text: Leisure travel surges through summer 2022 even as business travel remains depressed — the divergence our narrative traces between routes that recovered in passenger volume and routes that never came back.

text.headline: WHO Ends the Global Health Emergency
text.text: The WHO declares an end to COVID-19 as a global health emergency, more than three years after it began.

text.headline: National Passenger Volume Surpasses 2019
text.text: Across our ten metro areas, total annual passengers (437.9 million) finally exceed the 2019 baseline (424.7 million) — but as our recovery map shows, four of the ten metros individually had not.
